name: What is the difference between a tiny home and an ADU in California?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a tiny home and an ADU in California?

acceptedAnswer.text: In California, a tiny home can function as an Accessory Dwelling Unit (ADU) if it meets specific state and local requirements. An ADU is a secondary dwelling unit on a lot with an existing primary home. If a tiny home is placed on a foundation on a property with another existing residence, it would be considered an ADU. However, a tiny home can also be a standalone primary residence on its own lot, independent of another home. The classification affects zoning, permitting, and utility connections.
acceptedAnswer.description: A tiny home can be an ADU if it's a secondary unit on a lot with a primary home. Otherwise, it can be a standalone primary residence on its own lot, with different regulations.
